questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Iterator pattern?

options.text: Access the elements of a collection sequentially without exposing its underlying representation
Encapsulate a request as an object
Define how a set of objects interact
Ensure a class has one instance

questions.explanation: Iterator gives uniform sequential access while hiding structure. Request-as-object = Command; object interaction = Mediator; one instance = Singleton.

questions.prompt: What does an iterator's next() method return in JavaScript/TypeScript?

options.text: An object of the shape { value, done }
A boolean only
The entire collection
A deep copy of the collection

questions.explanation: The iterator protocol returns { value, done }; done becomes true when iteration finishes.

questions.prompt: An object is iterable if it has a [Symbol.____]() method returning an iterator.
questions.explanation: Symbol.iterator marks a class as iterable, enabling for...of, spread, and destructuring.

questions.prompt: How do generators simplify implementing the Iterator pattern?

options.text: A function* with yield automatically produces an iterator, so you don't hand-write next()
They make the collection a singleton
They deep-copy the collection first
They convert the collection to a different interface

questions.explanation: Generators create iterators automatically; you implement [Symbol.iterator] with a few lines of yield.

questions.prompt: Why is Iterator often called a pattern the language gives you 'for free' in TypeScript?

options.text: The iterator protocol is built in, so for...of and spread work once you implement Symbol.iterator
Because arrays cannot be iterated
Because it requires no code at all, ever
Because it only works on numbers

questions.explanation: The protocol is part of the language; you supply Symbol.iterator (often a generator) and the built-ins handle traversal.

questions.prompt: What advantage do generators give for large or infinite sequences?

options.text: They compute values lazily, so you only pay for the values you consume
They materialize the whole sequence up front
They guarantee a single instance
They encrypt each value

questions.explanation: Generators pause between values, enabling lazy and even infinite sequences without building the whole list.
